sentences.text: The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Mr.Harisha in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 14.05.2023 at about 9.30 p.m. deceased Harisha being pillion rider and one Ravi R.B., being rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517 were proceeding from Harohalli side towards Kaggalipura side and when they reached near Gabbadi lake, Gabbadi Village, Kanakapura-Bengaluru road, Harohalli Hobali,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that point of time, rider of said motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed.
As a result of which, the said bike skidded and toppled and caused the accident.
Due to impact of the accident, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.

3. Immediately dead body was shifted to CDSIMR Hospital, Devara Kaggalahalli,
Harohalli wherein post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over Nirmala.
B vs Ravi R.B
on 5 May, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
2 the dead body to the petitioners.
Subsequently, the petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

4. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale, healthy and aged about 24 years and working as Chopper at Kala Byraveshwara Chicken centre and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
5. It is contended that, the accident was occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517.
In this regard, Harohalli Police have registered the case against the rider of the said vehicle in Crime No.148/2023.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statements.
7. In the written statement the respondent No.1 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further denied the entire averments made in the petition.
Further stated that, he is the RC Owner of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
The rider had valid D.L. and policy was in force as on the date of the accident.
It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
8. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that,
driver
of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L as on the date of the accident.

It is the defence of respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself, as deceased himself was riding the motor cycle and it was a self-accident and not on the part of the rider of offending vehicle.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

3 9.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Harisha died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 14.05.2023 at about 9.30 p.m. near Gabbadi Lake, Gabbadi Village, Kanakapura-Bengaluru road, Harohalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y- 7517 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3) What order or award?
10. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.
11. On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined himself as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.

The Legal Manager of the respondent No.2 insurance company as RW2 and got marked the document at Ex.R5.
12.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

13. At the time of arguments the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the following decisions:
1. ILR 2021 KAR 146 between the Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.
Ltd., Belagavi Vs. Smt. Reshma and Others 2. ILR 2014 KAR 3336 between Branch Manager Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
Smt. Kempamma and Others 3. ILR 2009 KAR 2921 between Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. B.C. Kumar and Another.

14. On going through the supra decisions, the principles laid down in the supra decisions are that,
the MACT should not and ought not to place sole reliance on the judgment of the criminal court while considering the issue of the factum of the accident and the consequent negligence as stated in the claim petition filed before the criminal.
But the Tribunal will have to assess the evidence independently before any finding of the criminal court on the question of the driver pleading guilty.

Nirmala.B vs Ravi R.B on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
4 15.

My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative

,
 Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
16. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 51-Y-7517, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Harisha died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

17. On the other hand, respondent No.1 being the owner of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517 has contended in his written statement that, the accident occurred, due to imbalance, the pillion rider deceased himself suddenly fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.

18. Further the the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-Y-7517 has contended in its written statement that, at the time of alleged accident the deceased himself was riding a motor cycle and it was a self-accident, thereafter a false complaint was lodged, by creating a false story in order to get unlawful gain from this respondent.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

19. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the rider of the offending vehicle in question.
20. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Smt. Nirmala got examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.
. On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.148/2023 of Harohalli Police Station.
Ex. P2

-true copy of the first information statement given by petitioner No.1,
Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4- true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of IMV report,
Ex.P6- true copy of Inquest report, Ex.P7- true copy of PM report and Ex.P8-true copy of charge sheet.

Nirmala.B vs Ravi R.B on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
5 22.

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by petitioner No.1, the S.H.O. of Harohalli Police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y- 7517 for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 304(A) of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has submitted charge sheet against rider of the Motorcycle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 &
304(A) of IPC.
23.
On the contrary, the respondent No.1 being the owner cum rider of the motorcycle himself examined as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
In his cross-examination, he has deposed that on the day of the accident, there was raining, it means there was drizzling.
Further denied the suggestion that due to the over speed of riding the vehicle in the rain, Harish was died.
Further, admitted that he has not challenged the charge sheet.
24. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that, the deceased himself was rider of the motor cycle and due to his negligence accident occurred.
Further he has relied the supra cited decisions.
The respondent No.2 has examined its Legal manager as RW2, but his evidence will not much helpful to disprove the case of the petitioner.
Further the respondent No.2 has not placed any evidence to show that as on the date of accident deceased was riding the motor cycle.

25. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1 though several questions put to this witness, nothing has been elicited to disbelieve the assertion of the petitioners against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence it is crystal clear that, in connection with the above issue, evidence given by the petitioner No.1 is prevailing over the evidence of the respondents.
26. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing registration No. KA-51-Y-7517 and in the said accident, Harisha succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.2:
27.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P10 to Ex.P13 i.e., Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

28. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 being the wife has lost her husband and the petitioner No.2 being the daughter of the deceased has lost her love and Nirmala.
B vs Ravi R.B

on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
6 affection of her father, petitioner No.3 is the mother of deceased has lost her son, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
29. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P13 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 27.02.1997.
The accident occurred on 14.05.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 26 years.

For his age, multiplier '17' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
30.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as a Chopper at Chicken center and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/-
for the year 2023.
31.

Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

32. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."

Nirmala.B vs Ravi R.B on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
7 33.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are three persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
34. In the present case, deceased was aged about 26 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of below 40 years, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,92,000+76,800) = Rs.2,68,800/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,79,200/-
(Rs.2,68,800-Rs.89,600).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "17" which comes to Rs.30,46,400/-.
35.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

36. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.
37.

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.32,11,400/-
(Rupees thirty two lakhs eleven thousand and four hundred only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No. 103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. sentences.text: And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020 from the date of petition till its realisation.

LIABILITY:
39.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-51-Y-7517 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
40. As per Ex.R2, insurance policy bearing No.3005/273327475/00/000 was valid from 21.12.2022 to 20.12.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 14.05.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Hence,
respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition,
till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
41.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,11,400/- (Rupees thirty two lakhs eleven thousand and four hundred only) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Nirmala.B vs Ravi R.B on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
9
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for the share of 50%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 30% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 20%.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 3, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2, being minor,
entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank till she attains age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.
[ Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has submitted charge sheet against rider of the Motorcycle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 &
304(A) of IPC.
23.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
29. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P13 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 27.02.1997.
The accident occurred on 14.05.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 26 years.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
32. Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
Nirmala.B vs Ravi R.B on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44336732/
7 33.
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are three persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
34. In the present case, deceased was aged about 26 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of below 40 years, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C. owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The alleged accident had taken place on 14.05.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.

respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition,

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 3, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.2, being minor,
entire amount shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank till she attains age of majority.
After attaining the age of majority, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.

Draw award accordingly.
